patients.label: 30-year-old primigravida at 34 + 6 weeks’ gestation with PPROM and rapidly progressive hepatic and renal dysfunction with coagulopathy

identity_evidence.quote: we describe a 30-year-old primigravida at 34 + 6 weeks’ gestation

attribution_limitations: The reference point of "12 days after" for hospital discharge is not restated; the preceding clause gives ICU discharge six days after admission.
The referent of "complications" in "no subsequent reinfections or complications" is not specified.

The authors state the cesarean was prompted by renal deterioration, coagulopathy and lactic acidosis in the discussion, whereas the case text documents lactic acidosis in the ABGs after surgery and gives hepatic and renal deterioration as the reason.

The discussion states the absence of thrombocytopenia, while Table 1 prints platelet counts of 134 and 117 on postoperative days 1 and 2 against a normal range of 150-400; no timepoint is given for the statement.

The authors state liver and renal function improved steadily; Table 1 prints higher values on postoperative day 7 than on postoperative day 2 for gamma-glutamyl transferase (204 to 786 U/L), alkaline phosphatase (227 to 330 U/L) and AST (127 to 161 U/L).
The authors attribute the multiorgan dysfunction neither to PPROM nor definitively to any cause, and raise post-viral hepatic injury and transplacental contributions only as possibilities.

limitations: No figures and no supplements are listed in the source; no visual or supplement review applies.
The newborn son and the fetus are recorded inside the mother’s record with subject newborn or fetus, not as separate patients, because the source reports one individual case.
Table 1 values are recorded with their column headers as times and the printed normal ranges; no high or low flags were added because the table prints none.
Causal statements in the discussion (PPROM not causal, post-viral injury, transplacental contributions) are author interpretation and are not recorded as facts.
The reference point of the 12-day hospital discharge interval is not restated in the source.
